pronunciation.approximation: Say "morana" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Morana".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "morana" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Morana" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Morana
domains.subtitle: Winter
domains.lead: Morana is winter, death. The name means "Death" and belongs to the slavic tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name
cards.desc: The restoration Morana returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in slavic myth, cult, and cultural memory.

cards.name: Unicode Restoration
cards.desc: Preserved as a flagship temple despite the unregistrable plain-ASCII form.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.meaning: The restored form Morana, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.

mythology.lead: The stories of Morana place winter, death at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Morana appears in slavic tradition as winter, death. The name's meaning, "Death", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Morana in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Morana remains a touchstone for understanding slavic religion, art, and identity.
scholarlySources: Ivanits, Linda J., Russian Folk Belief (1989).
